symptomRule: A closed lid should stay within 30 degrees of its face slot plane and its source upper-lid direction should not invert relative to that plane.
method: Execute actual renderTo with closed-frame overrides, record actual Canvas affine matrices, and transform PCA axes from read-only source PNG ink. Exact scale uses headless support, which cannot change these orientation angles.

hypotheses.cause: Open-glyph alignment rotation is reused as the eyelid closing plane.
hypotheses.prediction: Keeping the source closed-lid angle and face slot rotation, but removing open-glyph fit rotation, removes the extra 31-degree tilt on circle_gap_02. Do not rotate the visible open eye to reach this frame; closing cels need separate registration.

hypotheses.cause: Mirroring alone creates the bad lid direction.
hypotheses.prediction: If this were the root cause, an unmirrored instance would be correctly oriented. Face09 eye_L is unmirrored yet tilts 33.36 degrees, so mirroring is an amplifier, not the initiating fault.

hypotheses.cause: The generated closed artwork itself is diagonal.
hypotheses.prediction: Its measured ink PCA should have the same large angle before any fit transform. Round source is near-horizontal, so this cannot explain face09; hook has a real gentle tilt that should remain.

hypotheses.cause: Face placement intentionally tilted the closing plane.
hypotheses.prediction: The final lid angle should agree with slot rotation plus source tilt. Face09 slots are approximately 2 and -1 degrees, excluding the observed mirrored 33-degree slopes.

limitations: The slot plane is a diagnostic baseline; some original closed arcs can intentionally curve the opposite way. Inverted travel flags are review candidates, not all proven defects.
No measured closed axes exceed 60 degrees; this run reproduces diagonal and inverted closure, not a fully vertical closed lid.
The directional test uses actual renderer transforms and actual source ink orientation. Source-contour scale fallback does not affect the measured angle.
